{
  "proposals": [
    {
      "title": "Multi-Chain Parallel MCMC for Rainfall-Runoff Posteriors",
      "field": "Bayesian calibration of rainfall-runoff models",
      "sequential_part": "Each Markov chain advances one candidate at a time: proposal, simulation, likelihood, and accept/reject depend on the previous state, so a single chain is strictly sequential.",
      "restructure": "Run many independent chains simultaneously on one or more GPUs, each chain on its own device or thread, with staged start points and a shared adaptation schedule; batch the per-chain accept/reject and proposal work.",
      "condition": "Independent chains must mix well enough that parallel chains provide usable effective sample size per chain, and GPU memory and bandwidth must hold many chain states without per-step communication.",
      "baselines": "A single long CPU MCMC chain from the same model, and a multi-chain CPU/MPI version; compare R-hat, effective sample size per chain, and posterior predictive intervals.",
      "first_test": "Time 8 or 16 independent chains on one GPU versus one CPU chain for 10,000 steps and report effective sample size per GPU-hour; roughly 30-60 GPU-minutes."
    },
    {
      "title": "GPU-Batched Surrogate Likelihood for MCMC",
      "field": "Rainfall-runoff model emulation and Bayesian calibration",
      "sequential_part": "Within one MCMC chain each likelihood evaluation calls a serial rainfall-runoff simulation over the full historical time series, and the chain waits on that simulation before proposing the next state.",
      "restructure": "Train a neural or Gaussian process surrogate offline on prior and posterior samples, then in MCMC compute batched likelihoods for many parameter vectors concurrently on the GPU, vectorizing surrogate evaluation across parameters and time windows.",
      "condition": "Surrogate error must be small enough over the posterior support that a correction stage or occasional full-model refresh preserves calibration; otherwise the resulting posterior is biased.",
      "baselines": "MCMC using the full physical model on CPU or GPU; compare parameter posteriors, prediction intervals, and distributional distance between surrogate and full-model posteriors.",
      "first_test": "Evaluate surrogate mean absolute error on 100 held-out full-model runs at posterior samples; roughly 10-30 GPU-minutes plus offline training time."
    },
    {
      "title": "Sequential Monte Carlo Tempering for Posterior Sampling",
      "field": "Bayesian calibration of rainfall-runoff models",
      "sequential_part": "Standard MCMC has a sequential tempering or adaptation path: each temperature level or adaptive step must finish before the next, making the chain a serial bottleneck even when many particles exist.",
      "restructure": "Use sequential Monte Carlo with many particles whose likelihood simulations are evaluated in parallel on GPU; propagate, reweight, and resample particles level by level, parallelizing the per-particle likelihood and proposal work.",
      "condition": "The particle set must remain diverse enough that resampling thresholds and enough particles prevent degeneracy, and the temperature schedule must be well tuned to avoid wasted GPU work.",
      "baselines": "A long adaptive MCMC chain and a parallel multi-chain MCMC sampler; compare effective sample size per GPU-hour, bias, and posterior predictive performance.",
      "first_test": "Run a 4-level SMC sampler with 2,048 particles versus a 2,048-step MCMC run and measure effective sample size per GPU-hour; roughly 1-2 GPU-hours."
    },
    {
      "title": "Time-Parallel Simulation of Runoff in Likelihood Evaluations",
      "field": "Computational hydrology and Bayesian rainfall-runoff calibration",
      "sequential_part": "The hydrologic model updates state through time step by step, such as soil moisture and routing, so a single forward simulation is a recurrence one answer waits on sequence after sequence.",
      "restructure": "Unroll the model over time and evaluate many parameter sets as a batch of recurrences on GPU; exploit parallelism over the batch dimension and, where possible, use associative scans or linearized operators to parallelize the time recurrence.",
      "condition": "The model recurrence must be expressible in differentiable batch form or approximated with controlled error, and the state dimension must be small enough to keep kernels resident and communication low.",
      "baselines": "Single CPU forward simulation and batched CPU evaluation; compare likelihood throughput, wall-clock per MCMC step, and final posterior error.",
      "first_test": "Benchmark one batched likelihood evaluation for 1,024 parameter sets against 1,024 sequential CPU evaluations, measuring wall-clock speedup and memory; about 20-40 GPU-minutes."
    },
    {
      "title": "Hierarchical Multi-Catchment Calibration as a Parallel Map",
      "field": "Regional Bayesian calibration of rainfall-runoff models",
      "sequential_part": "A single catchment chain is sequential as in MCMC, and updating shared regional hyperparameters can also require waiting for all catchment likelihoods to finish at each hierarchical step.",
      "restructure": "Parallelize independent catchment-level MCMC samplers over many GPUs or workers, then aggregate sufficient statistics for hyperparameters every K steps; use asynchronous or staged communication to keep workers busy.",
      "condition": "Enough catchments with independent data so per-catchment work dominates communication, network latency is low enough that aggregation does not stall chains, and the shared hierarchical structure is genuinely informative.",
      "baselines": "Sequential loop over catchments and a hierarchical MCMC on one CPU; compare posterior credible intervals, regional parameter estimates, and convergence diagnostics.",
      "first_test": "Run 20 catchment chains in parallel for 5,000 steps and compare wall-clock time and R-hat against 20 sequential chains; roughly 30-60 CPU/GPU-minutes."
    }
  ]
}
